subject: SIG/CAIQ evidence: proposed bucketed retention + customer-specific TTL exception
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Choi <security@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG/CAIQ evidence: proposed bucketed retention + customer-specific TTL exception

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the SIG/CAIQ review call earlier. Per your ask, we put together an initial evidence checklist and a minimal proposal for how HelixHealth-specific log retention could be carved out without impacting our platform-wide TTLs. The goal is to give you: (1) a short list of artifacts you can attach to your SIG submission, and (2) a narrow exceptional retention path for forensics/legal holds tied to HelixHealth tenant IDs.

Key points up front:
- We propose a "bucketed evidence" approach: production request logs remain on standard TTL (30 days), but HelixHealth can opt-in to a controlled evidence bucket for up to 180 days for a scoped subset of events (audit trails, authentication traces, and API request/response metadata).
- Access is limited to a named SRE/Legal pairing with audit logs and read-only exports; no additional replicas are created.
- Any extension requires a HelixHealth PO and documented legal hold (DocuSign or support ticket) and will be visible in our audit trail.

Attached: 20261201-helix-evidence-checklist.pdf (evidence mapping by SIG/CAIQ control) and a short one-page description of the bucketed retention concept.

Next steps: if this model looks reasonable, Marcus can produce the exact query filters and retention policy as a small config PR (I attached a sample spreadsheet). Can you confirm whether Helix's legal team needs a signed attestation before we enable the bucket?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: 20261201-helix-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Dr. Emily Choi <security@helixhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixHealth Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ evidence: proposed bucketed retention + customer-specific TTL exception

Naomi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear checklist. A few clarifying questions from our side:

1) "Scoped subset of events" — can you confirm the exact field names that will be included in the Helix evidence bucket? We need to map to our internal control matrix (authentication events, session start/stop, API call ids, and minimal payload hashes only).

2) Auditability — will Redwood provide a per-day export (CSV) of actions taken on the bucket (who accessed, export job ids)? That is a must for our SOC 2 auditor.

3) Legal hold workflow — Helix will require a formal sign-off timeline (we prefer 12 months max from hold creation, with renewals allowed). Is that supported operationally?

We reviewed the spreadsheet and left a few inline comments — the fields you flagged as "request metadata" look good, but we want to exclude any full request bodies or PII unless it's already redacted.

Victor from eDiscoveryPro will join our call next week to discuss export formats.

Thanks,
Emily
Dr. Emily Choi
Head of Security, HelixHealth

Attachment: 20261203-retention-buckets-proposal.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Choi <security@helixhealth.com>, Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@ediscoverypro.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ evidence: proposed bucketed retention + customer-specific TTL exception

Emily / Victor —

Answers inline below. Short summary at top.

Summary: We can support the Helix evidence bucket with a strict field-level allowlist (no full request bodies unless hashed) + daily access/export audit exports. Legal holds can be created for up to 12 months and renewed; we will require an approved Helix PO and a signed hold form.

Details:
1) Field names: the bucket will include the following fields (these are the exact column names from our logging schema): request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, auth_method, user_id_hash, session_id, route_path, response_status, latency_ms, payload_hash. We will explicitly exclude request_body and response_body from the bucket unless payload_hash is the only requirement.

2) Auditability: the platform will emit a daily CSV export (audit_access_YYYYMMDD.csv) to a customer-controlled S3 presigned location. The CSV contains user_email, action (view/export), object_id, timestamp, and job_id. Audit exports will be retained for 1 year per our standard audit log policy.

3) Legal hold workflow: we can create a named hold tied to Helix tenant ids. Requires: (a) Helix PO number; (b) signed legal hold form (template attached); (c) ticket in our compliance queue. Holds default to 12 months; renewals require a new PO and form.

Next steps: Marcus — can you produce the exact allowlist config and a sample audit CSV? Stephanie — I'll schedule a 30-min call with Victor and Helix legal next Tues to walk the export formats.

Thanks,
Naomi

Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2026 15:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ evidence: proposed bucketed retention + customer-specific TTL exception

Emily / team —

Attached is a short export sample (ediscopy) and the exact allowlist config we will apply if Helix signs the PO and the hold form. Notes:
- The allowlist is implemented as a tenant-scoped retention policy: helixhealth:retention_bucket=evidence_180d; filter = tenant_id=="helixhealth" && (event_type=="auth" || event_type=="session" || event_type=="api_request"); fields = [request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, auth_method, user_id_hash, session_id, route_path, response_status, latency_ms, payload_hash].
- Exports will be delivered as gzip CSVs to the pre-authorized S3 location you provide. Each export run will generate an audit_access file stored for one year.
- We will not create additional copies; the bucket is simply a retention policy variant on existing objects. Deletion will be automated at 180 days unless a renewal is approved.

If Helix legal confirms the acceptance language, we can spin this up in our staging tenant and provide the sample export link (will share a Drive link).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
